title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continuing from pp. 78-79): K is a number field, Gamma = Gal(K̄/K), and X is a hyperbolic curve, or more generally a variety embeddable in a semi-abelian variety. X_U seems to be a model over an open U of Spec O_K, so a point x in X_U means a rational point, i.e. a section over U. x0 is a fixed rational base point and pi^(x0) = pi_1^(X_K̄, x0), the profinite geometric fundamental group.

Galois acts on the torsor of étale paths pi_1^(X; x0, x). For a chosen path l : x0 -> x, the map u |-> f_l(u) (roughly l^{-1}·u(l), up to convention) is a continuous 1-cocycle Gamma -> pi^(x0). Its class f_{x0,x} in H^1(Gamma, pi^(x0)) does not depend on l. This is the nonabelian Kummer, or 'section', map X(K) -> H^1(Gamma, pi_1). The subscript 'nr' plausibly marks classes unramified over U.

Claim 1 is injectivity: x is entirely determined by f_{x0,x}, hence by the single cocycle f_l. Equivalently it is determined by g_{l^{-1}}, the cocycle attached to the reverse path l^{-1} : x -> x0, with values again in pi^(x0). The relation f_l = (g_{l^{-1}})^{-1} repeats formula (34) of p. 79.

The proof sketched on pp. 79/81 maps X to its Albanese or generalized Jacobian, i.e. a semi-abelian variety A. Mordell-Weil (plus Dirichlet's unit theorem for the torus part) makes A(K) finitely generated. So A(K) injects into its profinite completion, which injects into H^1(Gamma, T^A) via Kummer theory. Hence already the abelianized class (f_{x0,x})_ab separates points.

Claim 2 / programme: the 'explicit determination' of f_l, i.e. of the cocycle that 'constitutes' x, is called a very interesting and surely deep problem. Since Gamma itself is far from known, one must first say what 'determination' means. Proposal: an element u of Gamma is to be located (repéré) by its coordinates under the action on a profinite fundamental groupoid with several base points. Concretely these are the elements f_{l_j}(u) in pi^(x_j), or g_{l_j}(u) in pi^(y_j), for a finite system of generating arrows l_j : x_j -> y_j of the groupoid Pi_1(X, I), with x_j, y_j in a finite set I of base points.

On the next page Grothendieck hopes for 'explicit formulas' giving f_l(x) in terms of these parameters and of precise arithmetic invariants of x (in the Mordell-Weil-Néron situation). He says he has practically not started this work. By the injectivity argument, the first step reduces to the abelianized cocycles, i.e. to the analogous question for abelian or semi-abelian varieties.

Purpose: making the section-conjecture dictionary (rational points correspond to Galois sections or cohomology classes) effective and computable.
errors: No real mathematical error. Injectivity via Mordell-Weil needs X to embed in a semi-abelian variety (genus >= 1 via the Albanese; affine curves via generalized Jacobians plus finite generation of S-units). Grothendieck does state this hypothesis on p. 79.
Only the class in H^1 is canonical; the cocycle f_l depends on l up to coboundary. 'Determined by a single f_l' is correct but slightly redundant.

The meaning of the subscripts 'nr' and 'g' on H^1 is not explained on the page; they appear to denote unramified (or geometric-type) classes. The two subscripts may be inconsistent notations for the same thing.

ideas.what: A rational point is determined by its Galois cohomology class of path torsors (injectivity of the nonabelian Kummer/section map), proved via Mordell-Weil and the Albanese / semi-abelian embedding, already at the abelianized level
ideas.modern_name: Injectivity part of the section conjecture / Kummer map X(K) -> H^1(G_K, pi_1)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (letter to Faltings 1983); standard argument written e.g. by Nakamura, Stix
ideas.where_published: Letter to G. Faltings (27 June 1983), published in Geometric Galois Actions 1 (1997)

ideas.what: Encoding Galois elements u by their action on a finitely generated profinite fundamental groupoid with several base points, via coordinates f_{l_j}(u) on generating arrows
ideas.modern_name: Ihara/Drinfeld-style parametrization of Galois (e.g. sigma |-> (chi(sigma), f_sigma) in F^2, GT); fundamental groupoids with tangential base points (Deligne 1989)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara (1985-), Drinfeld (1990), Deligne (1989); Grothendieck, Esquisse d'un programme (1984)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984): multiple base points, Teichmüller tower; the precise coordinate proposal here is unsure

ideas.what: Programme: explicit formulas for the Galois cocycle of the path from a base point to a rational point x, in terms of arithmetic invariants of x; first step is the abelianized (Kummer/Albanese) part
ideas.modern_name: Explicit l-adic iterated integrals / l-adic polylogarithms of rational points; nonabelian Kummer map and Selmer varieties
ideas.where_published: Not found in Esquisse or the Faltings letter as an explicit-formula programme

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates, and explicitly leaves unstarted, a programme to compute explicitly the cocycle f_l (path from base point x0 to a rational point x). The cocycle is to be expressed in terms of the coordinates of Galois elements on a generating system of the multi-base-point groupoid, and of arithmetic invariants of x. This anticipates Wojtkowiak's and Nakamura-Wojtkowiak's explicit formulas for l-adic polylogarithms along paths from tangential points to z (whose abelian part is the Kummer characters of z and 1-z), and the nonabelian Kummer map in Kim's method. It is posed here for general hyperbolic curves and semi-abelian embeddings.
missed.quote: La détermination "explicite" d'un f_l ... est un pb très intéressant, et sûrement profond. ... il faut sûrement considérer qu'un u ∈ Γ est repéré par les éléments f_{l_j}(u) ∈ π̂_1(x_j)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a documented early (c. 1980-83) statement by Grothendieck of the explicit nonabelian Kummer map problem, with a precise proposal for what 'explicit' should mean (groupoid coordinates of Galois). It is of historical interest for crediting the origin of the l-adic iterated-integral / explicit Galois-cocycle programme. Beyond P^1 minus three points, the problem remains largely open for general curves.

deep.surprise_reason: The injectivity statement is well known from the Faltings letter. The explicit-formula programme with Galois 'coordinates' on a multi-base-point groupoid is a nice early formulation of what Ihara, Drinfeld, Deligne, Wojtkowiak and Kim later developed. It is only sketched, though, and its spirit is already visible in Esquisse.
transcription_corrections: Margin note '1-cocycle' refers to f_l : Γ -> π̂(x0), which fits the reading 'par la connaissance du 1-cocycle'.

The garbled duplicated lines 'pas bien précise ... explicite!) de f_l. Pour ceci, / la voie dite explicite !)' are a single passage, roughly: '"détermination" (pas bien précise — [?] dit. explicite!) de f_l. Pour ceci,'. The second line is a duplication.
Probable reading: 'Comme le groupe Γ bien sûr est loin d'être connu ... il faut préciser d'ailleurs en quel sens on entend une "détermination"'.
In the codomain of f_l the image shows π̂ with a crossed-out superscript, then (x0).
On the next page 'f_e' should read f_ℓ (ell, a path), not e.
